stem:
Poonam asks which shapes can tile the entire plane, covering without gaps or overlaps, rather than only a finite floor region.

Which claims are correct? Two options are correct.

options.text: Report the word tiling as the shape that covers the entire plane.
Repeated copies of a square can tile the entire plane.
Repeated copies of a regular hexagon can tile the entire plane.
Covering only a classroom floor with squares proves those squares tile the entire plane.

teacher.key_rationale: Squares and regular hexagons both tile the plane by repetition. Naming tiling as a shape, or treating a finite floor covering as a plane tiling, miss the entire-plane hinge.
